Job Title

Director of Engineering

Job Description Summary

Responsible to provide senior leadership and technical/operational support to Engineering teams across all regions. Also responsible for the development of policies and procedures pertaining to all types of buildings managed by C&W, including collaborating with market leadership to drive the performance of mechanical and engineering staff/systems and maintaining continuity to provide overall consistent product delivery and quality control for all properties.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities:

Develop and oversee the platform for property inspections and surveys, including policy compliance, energy audits and analysis, HVAC, energy management, electrical and plumbing systems. Also provide support for environmental compliance, ADA compliance, acquisition, third party surveys, and Property Condition Assessments
Act as a resource for all technical operations as needed to include system air and hydraulic balancing reports, boiler, chiller and cooling tower maintenance and performance; mechanical and electrical system noise, vibration control, tenant work orders and preventative maintenance, and equipment overhauls or replacements
Develop and maintain engineering and operations procedures to include preventative maintenance, energy management, water treatment, fire life safety, environmental health and safety, physical asset and team development, hazardous materials communications plan, indoor air quality programs, budget operating costs estimates, and comparisons
Drive compliance within the markets and region related to life safety programs and procedures, domestic water quality control, and water treatment programs to include EPA & OSHA compliance
Work with market leadership to evaluate prospective engineering employee qualifications, develop a network of engineering leaders, consult on manpower studies and establish career development track for engineers; responsible for ensuring completion of performance evaluations for direct reports
Deliver and coordinate operational and mechanical seminars for city-level and regional markets as well as building staff, as needed
Ensure sound construction management, project management, and commissioning best practices across the national portfolio
Where applicable, assist clients with due diligence and building evaluation efforts. Can participate in Integrated Design Teams as part of new development projects
Evaluate and recommend building automation systems, energy management/performance, and automatic temperature control systems
Provide value-engineering recommendations and evaluate contractor qualifications
Offer performance-related feedback and develop engineers for advancements; work with City Leads to identify engineers ready for new challenges and responsibilities
Responsible for the understanding and maintenance of national safety manual and providing feedback, as well as partnering with the EH&S group
Liaison with procurement in identifying national vendors, pricing, and local contract approvals. Also work to maintain key vendor relationship

Key Competencies

Communication Proficiency (oral and written)
Interpersonal Skills
Organization Skills
Technical Proficiency
Leadership

Education

High School Diploma or GED Equivalent

Important Experience

10+ years engineering experience with significant supervisory responsibility in a commercial property setting

Additional Qualifications

Vocational/Technical training certificate
Appropriate license/permit for trade as may be required, i.e. Journeyman or Master Electrician License or City Licenses
Universal Technician for CFC’s depending on market licensure requirements or any similar combination of education or experience
Knowledge and understanding of all applicable practices/techniques, laws, project controls and environmental regulations to include OSHA safety regulations
One or more of the following required: Local Operating Engineer’s License or Trade License, Systems Maintenance Administrator (SMA), Real Property Administrator (RPA)
Familiar with Energy Management System (EMS) programming and fire alarm systems
Basic Computing Skills in Outlook, Excel & Word

Work Environment

This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines. Regularly required to travel outside between properties in varying weather conditions.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee may need to travel from floor to floor, climb stairs, and may be required to travel outside between buildings in varying outdoor weather conditions. The employee may also be regularly required to remain in a stationary position (sit or stand) for 85% of the time; regularly use hands to operate office machinery and regularly required to walk, talk, and hear.

added.description:
About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including On Running, Breitling, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem.

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.

About The Role

We are hiring our first Director of Go-to-Market Engineering
.

Perk's revenue organisation is 800 people selling to more than 10,000 companies. Behind them sits a CRM, an enrichment and signal stack, a growing set of AI agents - and a lot of manual work that no longer needs to exist. Your job is to remove it and to build the automated systems that replace it.

You will own GTM Engineering end-to-end: which tools we use, how the architecture fits together, what gets built, and what it does for revenue. You report to the VP of Revenue Operations
, lead a small senior team across Europe and North America, and work across SDR, Account Executive, and Account Management - a few high-impact projects each quarter.

This is a player-coach
role, and we mean it. You will be in Clay, in the orchestration logic, in the agent workflows, building alongside a team doing the same. You're using your experience to guide and coach them to accelerate the pace.

The other half of the job is commercial. The best GTM engineers we have met can sit with a regional Sales VP, work out why their pipeline isn't converting, and leave with the right thing to build. That instinct matters more to us than any single tool on a CV.

What You'll Do

Own the strategy and the stack

Define Perk's GTM engineering architecture - how CRM, enrichment, signal, sequencing, orchestration and data layers fit together.
Make the tooling calls: what we adopt, what we consolidate, what we retire, and why it pays for itself.
Set the roadmap with the VP of Revenue Operations, Sales leadership, and the Revenue Systems and Data teams.
Establish the standards the team builds to - version control, documentation, testing, and rollback.

Build, hands-on

Design and build in Clay: tables, waterfall enrichment, AI columns, webhooks and API integrations in production.
Own the orchestration layer - the logic deciding which records enter a workflow, when, and on what criteria. This is where GTM automation succeeds or fails.
Build agentic workflows on modern LLM and agent tooling to take research, qualification, summarisation and data entry off people entirely.
Write the code the job needs - Python, SQL, SOQL or TypeScript.

Automate across SDR, AE, and AM

Own account prospecting automation globally: TAM sourcing, enrichment, ICP and intent scoring, prioritisation and distribution.
Give AEs their selling time back - CRM autofill, quoting, meeting prep, opportunity hygiene, first outbounds.
Build account intelligence for Account Management: risk signals, whitespace, account planning.
Take each project from prototype to production properly - instrumented and validated before it scales.

Bridge commercial and technical

Turn commercial problems into technical architecture, and technical output into impact a revenue VPs recognises.
Understand Perk's revenue goals and how to leverage AI capabilities for us to achieve them quicker and more efficiently.
Understand and drive clear and tangible commercial outcomes. For example, how to reduce the time that quota-carrying roles spend on non-core activities such as account research, be able to quantify the impact, and clearly communicate the outcomes to leadership.

Build the team

Lead and grow a small, senior team across Europe and North America.
Set clear ownership, and the review discipline that makes shipping fast also means shipping safely.
Grow the team's technical depth and commercial judgement in equal measure.

Experience

What Will Make You Successful

Deep background across Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, Sales Systems, Growth Engineering, or an adjacent technical commercial function in B2B SaaS
Proven track record in GTM Engineering specifically, with delivery at real scale — systems hundreds of sellers relied on, not a pilot for one team
Time as both a builder and a leader. This role needs both.

Technical craft

Clay expertise in production - complex tables, waterfall enrichment, webhook integrations and AI column logic that revenue teams actually depended on.
Deep Salesforce fluency: the data model, integration patterns, and where the constraints really are.
Working proficiency in code — Python, SQL, SOQL, TypeScript or equivalent. You pull your own data. Not all coding languages are necessary, but proficiency in one or some is required.
Architecture instincts: you build for scale, monitoring and recovery, not just for the first successful run.
Depth across several layers of the modern GTM stack - enrichment and data (Apollo, Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Cognism, PredictLeads), signal and intent (6sense, Bombora, UserGems), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), orchestration (n8n, Make, Workato), data infrastructure (Snowflake, dbt, BigQuery) and LLM and agent tooling. Nobody has all of it. We care that you have real depth somewhere and can learn the rest quickly.

Commercial instinct

You judge your work by whether it moved a commercial metric, not by whether it shipped.
You have the credibility with Sales leaders to scope the right build - and to say when automation is the wrong answer.
You understand the funnel end to end: TAM, ICP, pipeline generation, conversion, expansion, and the economics underneath.

Nice to have

Having stood up a GTM engineering function at a high-growth SaaS business, ideally above $100M ARR.
Experience taking an automation programme from pilot to global production, including what you learned when it got bumpy.
Multi-region GTM experience across EMEA and North America.

Why This Role

GTM Engineering is a discipline being written right now, and most companies are still treating it as a tooling function. This is the chance to own it properly, the stack, the architecture, the build, and the commercial outcome across a $300M+ revenue business with 800 people in the field, a genuine appetite for automation, and the budget and executive backing to move fast.

You would be the first person in this seat, with real systems and real data to work with rather than a blank page, and the freedom to decide what Perk's automation layer should look like. There is a lot to go after, the problems are interesting, and the impact is immediate and visible.

If you want to build the automation layer of a commercial engine at this scale and you want to still have your hands on it come and build it here.

What we offer:

Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk
Rest and recharge with our generous allocation of 20 vacation days and 12 public holidays
Enjoy the flexibility of three medical plans to choose from, with company contributions and an HSA when enrolling in an HDHP medical plan
Take control of your physical health with additional comprehensive benefit plans, covering dental, vision and Wellhub’s gym subscription from your start date
Rest assured that you’re covered by life and disability policies from your start date, with options to add extra protection through voluntary buy-up plans
Plan for your future with our 401(k) plan with company matching contributions
Care for your furry friends through partner discounts on pet insurance
Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party
Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones
Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave
Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes
Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year
Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years
Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support

Compensation
:

Compensation for this role is a combination of salary and stock options. The anticipated base salary range is $190,000 - $240,000 per year. Actual compensation may vary based on specific qualifications, experience, and other job-related factors.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

Compensation Range: $190K - $240K

added.title: Lead Director - AI Governance Engineering
added.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary

AI adoption across the organization is accelerating, and existing governance processes can add cycle time and rely heavily on manual review.

We are building an AI Governance Engineering capability to modernize governance through automation—shifting from approval-heavy workflows to registration-driven workflows with built-in controls, and continuous observability.

As Lead Director, AI Governance Engineering, you will create and lead a lean engineering team responsible for delivering governance-as-code:

platform-agnostic SDKs, APIs, and automated controls that help teams move faster while ensuring responsible AI guardrails are consistently enforced.

Key Responsibilities

Automated Use Case Intake & Risk Classification

Design unified intake APIs and user experiences that reduce friction and automatically populate metadata and integrate with application registration and provisioning workflows
Implement dynamic intake flows for ML, Generative AI, and agentic use cases.
Deliver automated inherent risk scoring and risk-based routing to provisioning and monitoring workflows.

Governance-as-Code Toolkits

Partner with AI Governance Data Scient to develop a platform-agnostic Python/SDK offering automated governance controls such as bias, drift, and AI safety testing.
Integrate governance checks into CI/CD pipelines so evidence is generated during development.

Enterprise Model & Use Case Registry Integration

Enable event-driven ingestion of intake data and model artifacts into the enterprise registry.
Support automated generation of audit-ready compliance artifacts and APIs for reviewers and auditors.

Self-Service Enablement & Automation

Expand policy-based routing for low- and high-risk AI use cases.
Automate proof-of-concept lifecycle patterns and accelerate access to approved AI environments.

Governance for Agentic Automation

Establish execution safety patterns for internal AI agents, including permission-scoped actions.
Partner with information security to implement runtime guardrails such as prompt filtering, data protection controls, and real-time observability.

Leadership & Collaboration

Build and lead a small, high-impact AI Governance Engineering team.
Partner with AI platform teams, governance, security, and privacy partners to embed technical controls into development workflows.
Define and track outcomes such as reduced intake complexity, faster cycle times, and improved governance transparency.

Required Qualifications

Experience leading software or platform engineering teams.
Strong system architecture skills across APIs, automation, CI/CD, and data platforms.
Experience building developer-facing tools such as SDKs, templates, or automation frameworks.
Familiarity with ML and Generative AI lifecycles and how governance controls can be validated through automation.
Ability to translate governance or risk requirements into scalable technical solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Responsible AI concepts such as fairness, transparency, explainability, and auditability.
Experience integrating automated quality gates into Git-based workflows and CI/CD pipelines.
Background working in regulated or high-trust technology environments.

Education

Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Analytics, Engineering, or related discipline. Master's degree preferred

What Success Looks Like

AI intake processes are simpler, faster, and largely automated.
Engineering teams have reusable SDKs and templates that make responsible AI the default.
Validation of controls shifts from self-reporting to automated checks and evidence.
Centralized observability provides real-time insight into AI usage, performance, and risk.

If you are excited about building trusted AI systems through practical engineering, we encourage you to apply—even if you do not meet every qualification listed. We value collaboration, learning, and curiosity.

Pay Range

The Typical Pay Range For This Role Is

$144,200.00 - $288,400.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

Great Benefits For Great People

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.

Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments.

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Engineering Manager to lead our Foundations

About East Daley

East Daley Analytics is building the energy market intelligence platform for professionals who need to understand how North American oil, natural gas, NGLs, infrastructure, producers, and midstream companies connect. Our mission is to drive transparency in energy markets by combining proprietary data, asset-level models, expert research, and workflow-ready software.
Our Energy Data Studio® platform helps customers forecast, compare, and analyze infrastructure and commodity performance across crude oil, natural gas, and NGL markets. It brings together operational and financial data, production forecasts, pipeline utilization, takeaway capacity, contract terms, counterparty risk, regulatory filings, dashboards, and exportable datasets.
We are looking for a CTO to help scale East Daley from a high-value research and data business into a category-defining energy intelligence platform.
The Opportunity

This is a hands-on executive technology leadership role for someone who has built and scaled complex data, analytics, AI, and SaaS products—ideally in markets where domain expertise, data quality, and customer trust matter as much as software velocity.
The right leader will inherit differentiated market expertise, proprietary models, a growing Energy Data Studio platform, and a team with deep knowledge of energy fundamentals. Your mandate is to transform that foundation into a scalable, modern, secure technology platform supporting product-led growth, enterprise data delivery, AI-enabled workflows, and faster innovation.
This role is for a technology leader who wants to be close to the business, customers, and product—not someone who wants to run a detached engineering organization.
What You’ll Own

You will own East Daley’s technology strategy, architecture, engineering execution, data platform, software delivery, and technical talent strategy. You will partner with the CEO, product, research, data, commercial, and customer teams to turn East Daley’s proprietary intelligence into software, data products, APIs, analytics workflows, and scalable customer experiences.
The core mandate includes:
Platform strategy and architecture

Define the technical roadmap for Energy Data Studio and related data products. Establish a modern architecture supporting dashboards, APIs, data exports, customer workflows, internal modeling, and AI-enabled capabilities.
Data platform and model operations

Build scalable systems for ingesting, validating, transforming, versioning, and distributing high-value energy data. Strengthen data trust, lineage, transparency, and repeatable model workflows.
Product-engineering execution

Create a high-performance engineering model with clear roadmaps, delivery discipline, release management, observability, documentation, QA, and customer feedback loops. Increase product velocity without compromising analytical accuracy or customer confidence.
AI and automation strategy

Identify practical opportunities for AI, machine learning, and automation to improve data ingestion, anomaly detection, research workflows, forecasting, customer interaction, search, summarization, and product experience. The approach should be pragmatic and commercially grounded.
Customer-facing technology leadership

Engage with strategic customers, prospects, and partners to understand workflow needs and translate them into product priorities. Demonstrate East Daley’s technical credibility to sophisticated energy, finance, infrastructure, and trading customers.
Team leadership and talent development

Lead and scale engineering, data engineering, platform, and technical product functions. Recruit senior talent, raise engineering standards, and build a culture where domain experts and technologists collaborate deeply.
Security, reliability, and enterprise readiness

Ensure the platform meets institutional customer expectations for security, access control, uptime, permissioning, auditability, vendor management, and scalable delivery.
What Success Looks Like

In the first 6–12 months, success will mean:
A clear technology strategy tied to business growth, product strategy, and customer value.
An executable Energy Data Studio engineering roadmap with improved release velocity, prioritization, and accountability.
Core data workflows that are more scalable, observable, documented, and less dependent on manual handoffs.
Engineering, data, product, research, and commercial teams operating from a shared roadmap.
Improvements in customer usability, performance, data access, APIs, visualization, and workflow integration.
A credible path toward useful, trusted, differentiated AI-enabled energy intelligence capabilities.

The Profile We’re Looking For

We are interested in leaders who have built sophisticated B2B data, analytics, SaaS, or market intelligence platforms and operated at the intersection of engineering, data, product, and commercial strategy.
You may be a fit if you have:
10+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including senior engineering, VP Engineering, CTO, or equivalent roles.
Experience building and scaling data-intensive products, analytics platforms, workflow software, market intelligence platforms, or B2B SaaS products.
A track record of leading engineering teams through scale, including architecture modernization, technical debt reduction, platform reliability, and product execution.
Strong fluency in data platforms, cloud architecture, APIs, analytics workflows, data pipelines, governance, and enterprise software delivery.
Experience partnering across product, research, commercial, and customer-facing teams to turn domain expertise into scalable products.
A pragmatic view of AI and automation and the ability to identify use cases that improve product experience, productivity, or data quality.
Credibility with technical teams and executives, with the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders.
A bias toward shipping and iterating while respecting East Daley’s commitment to accuracy, transparency, and analytical trust.

Energy experience is valuable but not mandatory. Curiosity and respect for complex domain expertise are mandatory.
Experience That Would Stand Out

Experience in energy, commodities, infrastructure, financial data, market intelligence, trading analytics, geospatial data, or regulatory data.
Experience building products combining proprietary and third-party data, forecasting models, visualization, and customer workflow tools.
Experience modernizing a founder-led or domain-expert-led technology organization while preserving what makes the company distinctive.
Experience scaling distributed engineering teams and building strong engineering culture.
Experience with data acquisition, entity resolution, time-series data, model versioning, BI/visualization, APIs, and customer-facing data delivery.
Experience commercializing AI/ML capabilities within a trusted B2B information product.

Why This Role Is Compelling

This is a rare opportunity to own technology for a business with real proprietary differentiation. East Daley is not building another generic dashboard product. We are building the system of record for energy market participants who need to understand asset-level fundamentals, infrastructure constraints, cross-commodity relationships, and financial exposure.
East Daley already has the domain expertise, models, customer trust, and proprietary data foundation. The CTO’s job is to turn that foundation into a platform that scales.
Compensation & Benefits

The anticipated base salary range is $250,000 to $300,000 annually
, depending on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated fit. The package also includes a target annual performance incentive of 20% to 30% of base salary
and comprehensive benefits. East Daley expects to hire within this range but may consider compensation outside it for an exceptional candidate.

401(k) with a 3% company contribution.
Flexible spending and health savings account options with company contributions.
Company-paid life, accidental death, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage.
Collaborative, in-person team environment in Greenwood Village, CO.
Dog-friendly office where team members may bring well-behaved dogs from time to time.

SVP of Product & Technology

About Plug

Plug is an automotive fintech startup building the marketplace for electric vehicles. Consumers, dealers, and commercial partners trade in, sell, and auction used EVs through a platform built exclusively for electric, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.

Consumers can get an instant cash offer in minutes, backed by data-driven pricing, battery state-of-health analysis, with pickup, payment, and title transfer handled end-to-end. Franchise and independent dealers across the United States bid in real time on inventory sourced directly from these consumers, dealers, and commercial partners. The result is a single platform that gives sellers a fast, fair exit and gives dealers a dedicated channel for sourcing used EV inventory.

Founded in 2023 and led by former Tesla executives, Plug has facilitated $100M in EV sales since launch and is backed by a $20M Series A from Lightspeed Venture Partners. We're building the most AI-native startup team in Los Angeles, full of operators, engineers, and ML researchers laying the transaction rails for the used EV market's exponential growth.

Why Plug

Here’s why you should be part of Plug:

You'll own a piece of the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.
You'll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.
You'll be part of an AI-native company. We're rethinking how work gets done at a fundamental level.
You'll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.
You'll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Head of Engineering to lead our engineering team and help shape the technical foundation of a fast-growing Series A company. You will report to the SVP of Product and Technology and partner closely to align on product vision and how that is executed by engineering.

This is a player-coach role. You will spend roughly half your time as an individual contributor - arbitrating architecture decisions, staying close to the systems, and individual contribution across features and tech debt - and the other half leading the team: setting direction, building engineering culture, collaborating on AI-native processes, and growing the organization.

The team is small, talented and moves fast. You will be stepping into an organization that has strong individual contributors and real technical momentum. Your job is to raise the ceiling - and to encourage what is working. We are looking to hire additional engineers, so you will be growing the team from day one.

We are building a culture that cares about collaboration, encourages intellectual honesty, celebrates technical excellence, and is driven by the company's goals. We believe diversity of perspective and experience are key to building great products and technology and a thriving team. Sounds cool? Let's work together.

Key Responsibilities

Set the technical vision and engineering direction for the team, working in partnership with the SVP of Product and Technology to ensure engineering strategy is tightly coupled to business goals.
Partner with the SVP of Product and Technology on product direction, roadmap sequencing, and technology strategy; own engineering execution and delivery against that plan.
Collaborate across functions - product, operations, and business leadership - to ensure engineering work is well-aligned, well-communicated, and measurably impactful.
Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing engineering team - setting a high technical bar, building a culture of ownership, and retaining strong individual contributors by keeping them challenged and autonomous.
Be an architectural leader - drive the evolution of systems architecture, make sound technology tradeoffs, and help the team navigate the balance between velocity and long-term maintainability.
Continue to be an individual contributor roughly half the time - writing code, reviewing pull requests at depth, and staying close enough to the systems to have real technical credibility with the team.
Systematically identify and reduce technical debt with a pragmatic, incremental approach.
Partner with the SVP of Product and Technology to build an AI-native SDLC - bringing hands-on experience with agentic coding tools, working with product to structure requirements and context that improve agentic results, and iterating on practices over time to get measurably better outcomes.
Own engineering team planning, recruiting, and growth.

Qualifications

8+ years of experience in software engineering, with 3+ years in an engineering leadership role where you continued to contribute directly to a production codebase.
Prior startup experience - has built or materially shaped an engineering function at an early-stage company where process was still being defined and priorities shifted regularly.
Currently contributing to a production codebase: writing code, reviewing pull requests at depth, and engaging with architecture decisions at the level of a strong senior engineer.
Has joined an existing engineering team with established contributors and a track record of building trust quickly, preserving contributor autonomy and momentum, and raising the bar without disrupting what is working.
Proficient in TypeScript with full-stack production experience across backend, frontend, relational databases, and API/webhook integrations. Our stack is TypeScript (Node.js + Next.js + React), Neon (cloud Postgres), Vercel, and AWS (ECS, S3, Redshift, Step Functions, Temporal). Experience with any of these is a strong plus.
Has built and managed systems that integrate deeply with HubSpot (or similar CRM) - treating it as a technical platform rather than just a CRM, including designing boundaries between HubSpot automation and application code to maintain system reliability.
Production experience with cloud infrastructure including infrastructure-as-code (Terraform), CI/CD pipelines, feature flags, and observability tooling - has made and implemented decisions in these areas without reliance on a dedicated DevOps team.
Deep, hands-on experience with agentic AI development - including working closely with product to structure requirements, context, and acceptance criteria that improve agentic coding results, and a track record of iterating on those practices over time to measurably improve outputs.
Has hired, grown, and retained engineering teams: a track record of scaling headcount thoughtfully while preserving culture and contributor quality.
Strong communication skills - able to represent engineering credibly to technical and non-technical stakeholders and write clearly and concisely.
Authorized to work in the US for any employer.
Prior experience in automotive, EV, marketplace, or fintech systems is a plus.

Compensation And Benefits

As new vertical pipeline matures, you will recruit, hire, and lead a team of Solution Engineers, with a defined path to formal people leadership of the SE organization. We are looking for someone who wants to earn that mandate by winning deals first, then scale themselves through a team.

Own the technical sale on our largest, most complex deals: Lead solution engineering activity for Flex's highest-priority opportunities in new verticals, from discovery and scoping through proof-of-concept, technical validation, and close.
Build trust with technical and executive buyers: Engage executive stakeholders at prospective partners. Translate Flex's capabilities into business outcomes that resonate at the board level and in the weeds equally.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

The world’s engineers are hungry to learn how to get the most out of Claude. At Anthropic, technical instruction is already happening everywhere: our Applied AI and Forward Deployed Engineering teams are teaching customers and partners, and engineers across the company are helping others learn to build with Claude. Today, that instruction is a shared responsibility, delivered alongside people’s primary roles. As demand grows, we need to turn that distributed expertise into a world-class technical instruction function.

You will build that function.

You will be the first person at Anthropic whose full-time job is technical instruction. You’ll spend your first year primarily in the room, teaching engineers, architects, and other technical practitioners, and build the people, standards, and systems that allow Anthropic’s technical instruction to scale far beyond the people we directly employ.

This is a player-coach role. You’ll lead sessions yourself, manage a bench of technical instructors, set the bar for what “ready to teach” means, and certify others to teach to that bar both inside and outside Anthropic. You’ll have real ownership: you’ll decide who is cleared to teach in Anthropic’s technical programs.

You’re an engineer who teaches and a teacher who has led other teachers. You can build an agent live in front of a skeptical engineer, diagnose what isn’t working in a technical lab, and make the material better. You can also watch an experienced instructor teach, identify what’s missing, and tell them their session isn’t ready yet, then coach them to get there.

Key responsibilities

Lead from the front: Deliver hands-on technical instruction across Anthropic’s onboarding and residency programs, from 12-person labs to 100-person field-readiness days. Set the tone for technical instruction by teaching regularly and modeling what excellent delivery looks like.
Build the instructor bench: Hire, onboard, manage, and develop technical instructors. Run the hiring loop, establish clear performance expectations, and make renewal and conversion decisions against criteria you define.
Set the quality bar: Define what excellent technical instruction looks like at Anthropic. Create and maintain the observation rubric, dry-run protocol, and cleared-to-teach process that every instructor-led technical session must meet.
Scale through certification: Design and run train-the-trainer programs for internal experts, contract instructors, and facilitators from our training partners. Assess instructors against Anthropic’s technical delivery standards and certify those who meet the bar, enabling instruction to scale beyond our employees.
Turn expertise into great instruction: Partner with Technical Enablement Leads to transform technical content into sessions, labs, and exercises that work in a live room. Bring back what you learn from teaching to continuously improve the content.
Enable programs without owning them: Partner with our onboarding and Training & Certification teams to staff programs with cleared instructors. Own the quality of instruction within those programs, even when the broader program sits elsewhere.
Measure and improve: Establish meaningful measures of learner outcomes and instructor quality. Review results at the session and instructor level, identify where instruction is falling short, and act on what you learn.

Minimum Qualifications

8+ years of relevant professional experience across software engineering, solutions engineering, developer advocacy, technical education, or related technical roles.

People leadership: You have managed instructors, trainers, developer advocates, solutions engineers, or similar technical practitioners, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and development. You have continued teaching or delivering technical content while managing others.
Instructor development: You have designed or run a train-the-trainer program, instructor certification process, observation framework, or comparable system for evaluating and improving instructor quality.

Experience managing a contractor or vendor-supplied instructor bench, or certifying instructors across regions from recordings or through trained observers
